why: I compared the builder brief's steps with the verifier brief. Running `npm test` (step 5) is allowed because an expect line names it, and the new unit test in step 3 is allowed because the builder writes it. Step 5 also tells the builder to run `printf '{port: 9000' > /tmp/bad.json && node src/app.js /tmp/bad.json` and confirm that a stderr warning appears, the app prints `listening on 8080`, and it exits 0. The verifier brief's advisory uses the same probe: the same `{port: 9000` input written with printf, then "try `node src/app.js /tmp/verify-bad.json`" to check for a stderr message naming the path. Neither the issue nor its expect lines name this command, so it is a verifier probe passed on to the builder. That breaks the rule that the builder brief carries no probe that also appears in the verifier brief.
